license.payload: Public domain: the works are of 1844–1873; the manuscripts are nineteenth-century copies; the lithographs are of Bombay, c. 1882 and 1893; Tumanskii's edition (St. Petersburg, 1899) and Browne's editions (Cambridge, 1891; Leyden and London, 1910) were published before 1931. The Iran National Baha'i Archives volumes are photostat reproductions of manuscripts (issued in Iran in the 1970s, each with a typed title sheet); H-Bahai's digital reprints are facsimiles of those volumes and of the lithographs and states no licence of its own; a facsimile of a public-domain work adds no authorship. Internet Archive scans (Digital Library of India) of the Browne volumes.
license.record: CC-BY-4.0 applies to this seat record only.

normalization: Scans and images as fetched: the manuscripts and lithographs have no text layer and the scan is the text; their loci are read from the scan and recorded with the page. The two Browne volumes carry the Internet Archive's OCR text layer as fetched, uncorrected (text/<slug>.ocr.txt). Internet Archive files checked against the Archive's md5.
units: one scan (PDF or page images) per work, with an OCR text layer where the Internet Archive supplies one
scope: Both sides of the tradition that began in Shiraz on the night of 22–23 May 1844, when the Bab declared his mission to Mulla Husayn and began the Qayyum al-Asma'. The Bab: the Qayyum al-Asma' (Ahsan al-qisas) in the copy given by Mulla Husayn, the Persian Bayan, and Panj Sha'n, in the Iran National Baha'i Archives manuscripts. The division after him: Baha'u'llah's Kitab-i Iqan in the first lithograph (Bombay, c. 1882) and the Mishkin Qalam lithograph (Bombay, 1893), al-Kitab al-Aqdas in Tumanskii's St. Petersburg edition (1899), and 'Abdu'l-Baha's Traveller's Narrative in Browne's facsimile of the Persian (1891), on the Baha'i side; and the Kitab-i Nuqtatu'l-Kaf in Browne's edition (1910), the history Browne attributed to Hajji Mirza Jani and read as the Azali account, an attribution Baha'i scholarship disputes. Not seated: the UCLA manuscript of the Persian Bayan (a 199 MB scan, over the repository's file limit): QUEUED; the Arabic Bayan, found only in a 1962 printing; writings of Subh-i Azal in his own name, not found in an open edition in this pass: QUEUED; the Kitab-i Aqdas in the Tehran printing of c. 1943 that H-Bahai reproduces beside Tumanskii's; translations.
why_seated: The second tradition of 1844: the Bab declared his mission in Shiraz on 22–23 May 1844, five weeks before Joseph Smith was killed; after the Bab's execution (1850) his followers divided between Subh-i Azal and Baha'u'llah, as the Latter Day Saints divided between the Twelve and Strang.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 27 October 2026: "need to seat the book of mormon but im not doing it without several diverging simultaneous traditions in the batch" — offered the traditions that divided in 1844 (the Latter Day Saint succession, the Bab's declaration, the Millerite disappointment, the Taiping beginnings), or the Book of Mormon's own editions — "1. definitely. lets go."
contested: The Nuqtat al-Kaf's authorship and date (Browne: Hajji Mirza Jani of Kashan, 1850–52) and the ascription of the INBA vol. 1 sahifas (H-Bahai's index: Subh-i Azal; the volume's title page: the Bab) are recorded as their sources state them.
